_comment: Post-deploy proof that proxy/wrangler.jsonc is ACTUALLY IN EFFECT in production.
SAFETY — this Worker fronts a paid API and an atomic credit ledger, so every probe
below is read-only, unauthenticated, and cannot spend a credit or mutate a balance:
* /v1/label is NEVER probed — it calls Claude and costs ~$0.01 per request.
* /admin/* is probed ONLY without credentials, where requireAdmin() returns 401
before touching KV or the Durable Object.
* the bearer token below is deliberately not a real token. It is well-formed so it
gets past the header check and forces a KV read, and unknown so the lookup misses.
WHY /health IS NOT ENOUGH, and is included anyway: the router answers GET /health
with a static object and touches no binding at all. It is the exact shape of check
that would stay green through the outage this probe exists to catch. It earns its
place only as a discriminator — if /health is also down, the Worker is not deployed,
which is a different problem from a binding that did not resolve.
originIsCanonical: no custom domain is configured — the extension's manifest.json host permission names this exact workers.dev host, so it is production

probes.name: the Worker is deployed at all (static route, touches no binding — a discriminator, not a config check)
probes.whenMissing: a non-200 here means the Worker itself is down or unrouted; every probe below would also fail, for a reason that has nothing to do with the config. Verified 2026-07-30 against a runtime with the KV binding removed: this route still answered 200 {"status":"ok"}. That is the whole point of keeping it separate from the deep check below.

probes.name: TOKENS and CREDITS both resolved — deep binding liveness, no credential needed
probes.whenMissing: 503 {"status":"degraded"} naming the unavailable binding. This is the only probe that reaches the Durable Object, because every other CREDITS path sits behind a real token. It uses a reserved, never-funded sentinel account (__binding_probe__) and a deliberate KV miss, so it holds no credential and can spend nothing. If this 404s, the deep endpoint is not deployed yet — run `npm run deploy`.

probes.name: TOKENS (KV) resolved — an unknown-but-well-formed token forces a real KV read and misses
probes.whenMissing: 403 is only reachable AFTER env.TOKENS.get() returns null. If the KV binding did not resolve, the property access throws and the router's catch returns 500 {"error":"Internal error"} — note 500, NOT 503, so a probe written to look only for 503 would miss this entirely. A 401 instead would mean the Authorization header never parsed, i.e. a different bug.

probes.name: admin surface stays fail-closed without credentials
probes.whenMissing: anything other than 401 on an unauthenticated admin call is an auth regression, not a config problem — a 200 would mean anyone can mint tokens against a paid API key. requireAdmin() runs before any binding is touched, so this probe cannot mutate state. It deliberately does NOT claim to prove ADMIN_SECRET is set: a missing secret also yields 401, so the two are indistinguishable from outside.

probes.name: unrouted paths 404 as JSON from the Worker, not from Cloudflare's edge
probes.whenMissing: an edge-shaped HTML 404 here means requests are not reaching this Worker's fetch handler at all — routing, not config.

_unproven: CREDITS is now proven, by GET /health?deep=1 — WITHOUT a credential.
The earlier plan here was to mint a zero-credit probe token, store it as a repo secret,
and send it to /v1/balance. That works, but it creates a standing credential whose only
job is to be observed: something to store, scope, rotate, and leak. The cheaper answer was
to make the binding observable instead of making the observer privileged — a deep health
route that does a deliberate KV miss and reads the balance of a reserved, never-funded
sentinel account. It holds nothing, can spend nothing, and needs no secret in CI.
STILL UNPROVEN, and the runner will keep saying so: MODEL and DEFAULT_STARTING_CREDITS.
MODEL is only observable by paying for a labeling call; DEFAULT_STARTING_CREDITS only by
minting a token. Neither is worth a probe that costs money or mutates state, and both are
low-consequence if stale — a wrong MODEL degrades label quality, it does not break the
service. Recorded as a deliberate accepted gap rather than an oversight.
